adv.subtitle: Server Settings
adv.desc: Control rate limiting, message filters and monitor system status in real time. Changes apply immediately to the backend.
adv.rlHowP1: During an active live, dozens of messages per second can arrive. Without limits, the TTS queue would grow uncontrollably and the bot would accumulate minutes of delay.
adv.rlHowP2: Rate limiting acts as a server-side filter: it decides how many TTS requests are allowed in a time window. If the limit is exceeded, additional requests are rejected with error 429 and the message does not enter the voice queue.
adv.rlHowP3: It is DISABLED by default. Enable it only if you see the bot saturating or if Google TTS starts giving errors due to too many requests.
adv.rlHowP4: Practical example: with 10 requests / 5 seconds, if 20 messages arrive in 5 seconds, only the first 10 will be read. The rest are silently discarded.
adv.rlToggleHint: Disabled by default. Only enable it if the live has a lot of spam or TTS gets saturated.
adv.a11yDesc: Visual and audio settings for reading and reduced motion
adv.a11yHowP1: Some overlays use continuous animations (glows, bounces) that can bother people with motion sensitivity or photosensitivity. "Reduce motion" turns them off across all OBS overlays.
adv.a11yHowP2: Text size enlarges the whole app (main window, this screen and the OBS chat overlay), not just chat. Slow speech turns on a more paced reading mode in the TTS.
adv.a11yReduceMotionHint: Turns off animations for alerts, followers, likes and gifts in OBS overlays.
adv.a11ySlowSpeechHint: TTS voice reads more slowly. Useful for processing audio better.
adv.a11yHighContrastHint: Strengthens borders and secondary text in the main window for better readability.

modTour.introDesc: Every viewer who interacts with your streams is registered here. From this table you control who can talk and who the TTS reads. This is in-app moderation: it does not ban on TikTok, Twitch or YouTube.
modTour.tabsDesc: Someone becomes a Follower in two ways: they follow you while you're connected, or you mark them by hand. The app can't ask the platform for your follower list, so anyone following you from before shows up under Non-followers until you mark them.
modTour.statsDesc: How many people are registered, how many are followers, and how many have an active penalty right now.
modTour.filtersDesc: Search by name, filter by platform or state (muted, banned, no penalty), and sort by recent activity or name.
modTour.tableDesc: On each row: Mute (still visible in chat, but TTS skips them), Ban (their messages don't even show up), ★ to mark as follower, Clear penalties, and ✕ to drop them from the registry. Temporary penalties expire on their own, even with the app closed.
modTour.chatMenuDesc: You don't have to come here: click anyone's name in the live chat and the same menu opens — mute, ban, mark as follower or block a word.
modTour.toggleDesc: On, the TTS reads everyone. Off, it only reads followers and whoever you marked by hand; the rest still show up in chat, just without a voice. Careful on day one: with an empty registry you silence almost your whole audience.
modTour.blockedDesc: Copy the annoying word from chat, hit this, paste it and it's blocked — without leaving the view or reconnecting. The window stays open so you can paste several in a row. Messages containing it are ignored entirely.
modTour.scrollDesc: The chat no longer chases the newest message but the one the TTS is reading, which usually lags a few messages behind. Scroll up and it stays put so you can read; return to the bottom and it resumes on its own.

blockWord.title: Block a word
blockWord.desc: Paste or type the word and you're done: the server applies it instantly, no reconnecting. You can keep adding without closing the window.

soundTour.introDesc: Upload sound effects and play them with a click or a keyboard shortcut, even while the app is fullscreen.
soundTour.uploadDesc: Click here to upload an audio file (mp3, wav, ogg, webm, or m4a). You can have up to 24 sounds in your pad.
soundTour.testDesc: Use this button to check that your system audio is working before playing your sound effects.
soundTour.shortcutDesc: In this window you pick an icon from the full gallery, the card color, the keyboard shortcut (Ctrl/Alt/Shift + key), and you can delete the sound.
soundTour.deckDesc: Each card is a sound. Left-click plays it; right-click opens its settings.
soundTour.limitDesc: You can upload up to 24 sounds total. This counter shows how many you've used.

botTour.introDesc: Your chat can request songs by typing !p song name or pasting a YouTube link. From here you control everything: what's playing, the queue, and who's allowed to request.
botTour.nowPlayingDesc: Turn on the !p command with this switch. From here you can also pause, skip the current song, and adjust the music volume (separate from the TTS volume).
botTour.queueDesc: Songs requested by chat pile up here in order. You can clear the queue anytime with the Clear button.
botTour.playlistDesc: Add your own list here (one song or link per line). It plays on loop when there are no chat requests — turn it on and save so it starts.
botTour.settingsDesc: Adjust the cooldown between requests per user, the max songs allowed in queue, and ban users who abuse the !p command.

voiceTour.introDesc: Set up the voice that reads chat: language, speed, volume, and which messages get read based on their language.
voiceTour.voiceDesc: Pick the language and accent for the TTS voice. 13 options (Spanish, English, Portuguese, French, German, Italian, Japanese, Chinese, Russian, Korean). Changing it also affects the language filters below.
voiceTour.testDesc: Type any text and hit Test to hear how the selected voice sounds, no chat connection needed.
voiceTour.rateDesc: Adjust how fast the TTS talks. Applies in real time to the next message read.
voiceTour.volDesc: Controls TTS volume independently from the bot's music volume.
voiceTour.charFilterDesc: When on, messages written with characters that don't match the active voice's language are ignored (e.g. blocks Chinese or Japanese if your voice is Spanish).
voiceTour.wordFilterDesc: Finer dictionary-based filter: only reads messages written in the active voice's language, plus any extra languages you allow below. Names or typos don't block the message.
voiceTour.dictModalDesc: Choose which extra languages, besides your voice's, are allowed for the TTS to read. Close this window to continue the tutorial.

shortcutsTour.introDesc: Set up global keys to control TTS and the bot's music without touching the app, even with another window focused.
shortcutsTour.pauseBtnDesc: Pause or resume reading chat with one click. Handy to mute quickly without disconnecting anything.
shortcutsTour.pauseKeyDesc: Click the field and press the combo you want (with Ctrl/Alt/Shift), or use the F8 / Play-Pause key presets.
shortcutsTour.skipDesc: Assign a key to skip the message currently being read (default F9).
shortcutsTour.clearDesc: Assign a key to wipe the whole pending TTS queue at once (default F10).
shortcutsTour.musicPauseDesc: Shortcut to pause or resume the music requested by chat via the !p command (default F11).
shortcutsTour.musicSkipDesc: Shortcut to skip the song currently playing in the music bot (default F12).

clipsTour.introDesc: Mark the exact moment something fun or important happens while you're live, so you can find it later and cut the clip without scrubbing through the whole recording.
clipsTour.startDesc: Before you can mark clips you need to start the timer here. It's the reference point for every marker (00:00:00 onward).
clipsTour.markDesc: Once the stream is running, this button activates. Click it at the right moment, or press Ctrl+Shift+M — the shortcut works anytime, even with the app minimized.
clipsTour.obsDesc: If you connect OBS via WebSocket here, every clip you mark also automatically saves the OBS replay buffer, in addition to the marker in the app.
clipsTour.historyDesc: Every clip you mark is listed here with its elapsed time and real timestamp, so you can later find those moments in your recording or in OBS.
clipsTour.mobileDesc: Scan this QR code, open Control in the mobile panel, and tap Mark Clip. The button becomes available after you start the timer in the app.

pluginStoreTour.introDesc: Here you choose which tools to show in the sidebar and in what order. Chat and Settings are always available, everything else is up to you.
pluginStoreTour.gridDesc: The badge tells you if it's Visible or Hidden in the sidebar. Click a card to see its details.
pluginStoreTour.dragDesc: Grab any card and drop it on another to reorder them, Trello-style. The new order updates the sidebar instantly.
pluginStoreTour.mediaDesc: A sample image or video of the tool goes here, once available.
pluginStoreTour.headerDesc: The tool's name and a short description of what it does.
pluginStoreTour.actionsDesc: "Open" takes you straight to the section even if it's hidden. The green button adds or removes it from the sidebar.
pluginStoreTour.aboutDesc: A fuller explanation of how the tool works.

overlaysTour.introDesc: Each card generates a unique URL for a different overlay. Paste it into OBS as a Browser Source and it updates live on its own.
overlaysTour.urlDesc: This is the address you'll copy and paste into OBS. It updates automatically whenever you change the color, opacity, or other card options.
overlaysTour.copyDesc: Click "Copy" to grab the URL. Then in OBS: Add Source → Browser → paste the URL → enable "Enable transparent background".
overlaysTour.customizeDesc: Adjust the accent color, background opacity, and other options. Changes apply instantly to the URL, no need to reload OBS.
overlaysTour.testDesc: Use the "Test" button to trigger a sample alert and preview it in OBS before going live.

chatActionsTour.skipDesc: Cuts off the message being read right now and moves to the next one in the queue.
chatActionsTour.emergencyDesc: Instantly mutes chat, likes, joins, and shares. Keeps only gift alerts and new follower announcements active.
chatActionsTour.clearDesc: Clears the on-screen chat log and empties the TTS queue. It doesn't affect messages already sent by viewers.
chatActionsTour.blockedDesc: Opens the blocked words editor to manage which terms get filtered out before being read aloud.
chatActionsTour.togglesDesc: Turn each event on or off individually: comments, gifts, joins, follows, likes, shares, and whether the sender's name gets announced.
chatActionsTour.ttsDesc: Turn it off to instantly mute the voice and clear the queue. Turn it back on whenever you want reading to resume.
chatActionsTour.connectDesc: This is the real button that connects your saved channels (TikTok/Twitch/YouTube) to the live chat. Without this, nothing above has any effect.
chatActionsTour.logDesc: Messages show up here as they arrive, with a platform badge and status (read, muted, etc.).

about.overlays: Overlays are pasted into OBS as a Browser Source and show gifts, likes and new followers from your stream in real time. Each one has its own URL you can copy and customize colors, sizes and animations.
about.clips: Bookmark the exact moment of a highlight with a keyboard shortcut while you're live, without cutting the stream. Review the bookmark list afterward to quickly find where to cut the clip.
about.soundpad: Upload your own sound effects and assign a keyboard shortcut (with a Ctrl/Alt/Shift modifier) to play them instantly, even with the game in fullscreen.
about.mobile: A lightweight panel you open from your phone on the same WiFi network as your PC. Pause the TTS, skip messages and control the essentials without going back to the computer.
about.bot: Chat requests songs by typing !p followed by a name or a YouTube link. Your own playlist plays in the background when there are no requests. Configurable with a cooldown and queue limit.
about.moderacion: Keeps a local history of every viewer who chatted or followed you, with the option to mute them (message shows but isn't read aloud) or ban them (message never shows). It doesn't touch their account on the real platform.
about.mcp: MCP (Model Context Protocol) exposes the app’s features as tools for an AI agent. With Claude Code or Claude Desktop connected, the agent can read chat, moderate viewers, control music and check stream state. The endpoint only works from this computer, and destructive actions (ban, disconnect) sit behind a separate permission.

chatGuard.title: Chat moderation
chatGuard.desc: Decide which messages are shown and read aloud.
chatGuard.enableDesc: Catches insults and unwanted messages, even when they are written with tricks. Your blocked words list always applies.
chatGuard.peopleNote: Muting and banning individual people keeps working even if you turn this off.

level.title: Protection level
level.softDesc: Only the most obvious. Almost never blocks by mistake.
level.balancedDesc: Recommended. Blocks the clear cases and attempts to get around the filter.
level.strictDesc: Also blocks doubtful cases. It may stop harmless messages.

custom.tricksHint: For example with symbols, spaces or repeated letters.

mode.title: What should the filter do with what it detects?

mode.enforceDesc: Messages the filter detects are not shown or read aloud.

lang.title: Filter languages
lang.hint: Messages in other languages are not filtered by words. This does not change the voice language.
lang.minOne: Keep at least one language on.
lang.auto: Automatic, based on the TTS voice
lang.autoHint: The filter uses the voice's language plus English and updates by itself when you change the voice.

words.title: Words
words.blockedHelp: Messages with these words are not shown or read aloud. This list always applies, even if the advanced filter is off.
words.allowedHelp: These words are never blocked, even if the filter detects them.
words.allowedSingleWord: Only single words are accepted here, not phrases.
words.duplicate: It is already in the list.
words.conflict: That word is already in the {other} list. Remove it from there first.
words.emptyBlocked: There are no blocked words yet.
words.emptyAllowed: There are no allowed words yet.
words.truncated: Showing {shown} of {total}. Use the search to see the rest.

status.title: Filter status
status.loadError: The filter could not be checked.
status.unavailable: The advanced filter is not available in this installation. Your chat keeps working with the basic filter.
status.error: The filter has problems. We are using the basic filter; your chat keeps working.
status.okShadow: Working in test mode: it warns but blocks nothing.
status.okEnforce: Working: it blocks what it detects.

people.note: To mute or ban a specific viewer, use Moderation.

toast.saveError: The change could not be saved. Try again.

queueBadge.droppedHint: Messages dropped because the voice queue was full. Moderation did not block them. Click to learn more.
queueBadge.blockedHint: Messages moderation blocked or muted in this session. Click to see the list.
queueBadge.shadowHint: Messages the moderation engine would have blocked, but they went through because it is in notice mode. Click to see them.

blocked.intro: Messages that automatic moderation blocked or muted since you opened the app. They are kept in memory only: they disappear when you close the app.
blocked.filter: Filter by user, text or reason
blocked.summary: Blocked or muted: {blocked} · Detected in notice mode: {shadow}
blocked.empty: No messages have been blocked yet in this session.

words.intro: Words you block on your account. You can add or remove them in Settings > Chat moderation.
words.empty: You have not blocked any words yet.
words.error: Could not load the list. Try again in a moment.
words.dictionaryNote: Besides your list, the moderation engine uses a dictionary of thousands of words that are not listed here.

queue.explain: When more messages arrive than the voice can read, the queue fills up and new ones are discarded. This has nothing to do with moderation: these messages simply did not fit in the voice queue.
queue.dropped: Discarded because the queue was full
queue.tip: You can skip the current message or clear the queue from the chat controls.
